best_for: Minecraft modders, resource-pack makers and pixel-art 3D artists who want boxy low-poly models with painted textures and animations, free.
description:
Blockbench is a model editor for low-poly 3D models with pixel-art textures, made by the developer JannisX11. Its website lists Mojang Studios, Hytale and Noxcrew among the studios that use it. The interface is meant to be easy for beginners, with deeper options for experienced 3D artists.

You can build a model from cuboids for the classic Minecraft look, or switch to the mesh tools for more complex low-poly shapes. For color, you can make your own palettes or import one, and draw shapes straight onto a texture. The website has a gallery of finished models you can turn around in 3D, and it runs contests if you want to show your work.

points.title: Made for Minecraft, not only for it
points.text: There are dedicated formats for Minecraft Java and Bedrock Edition. Models can also go out in standard formats for rendering, 3D printing or game engines.

points.title: Paint right on the model
points.text: You can paint textures directly on the 3D model or in a 2D editor, auto-generate UV maps, or hand the texture to your own pixel-art program.

points.title: Animation included
points.text: An animation editor handles rigging and position, rotation and scale keyframes, with a graph editor for easing.

points.title: Plugins fill the gaps
points.text: A built-in plugin store adds tools, export formats and generators, and plugins are written in JavaScript if you want to make your own.

points.title: Free, GPL, no account
points.text: Blockbench is open source under GPL 3.0 and free for any project. A web app version also runs in the browser if you cannot install software.

points.title: Install notes
points.text: The Windows installer is x64 and installs for the current user, so no admin rights are needed. Macs get separate Intel and Apple silicon builds for macOS 12 and later. The Linux Flatpak is verified on Flathub but x64 only. Windows keeps 63 versions; macOS and Linux list only the current release.
